repair.why_wrong: Calls in Advance refers to money paid by shareholders before the company actually calls for it, not unpaid amounts.
repair.key_idea: Calls in Arrears are specifically the called-up capital that shareholders have not yet paid, distinguishing it from calls in advance or other types of capital.

repair.why_tempting: Option 3 looks right because redeemable preference shares are common, so one might think preference shares are always redeemable.
repair.why_wrong: Preference shares having preferential dividend rights is true regardless of redeemability. Redeemability is unrelated to dividend preference.
repair.key_idea: Preference shareholders get dividends before equity shareholders by definition; redeemability is a separate feature and not always true for preference shares.
repair.next_step: Review the definitions of preference shares and redeemable shares to clearly separate dividend rights from redeemability.

repair.why_wrong: Paid-up capital is based on the nominal value of shares, not the repurchase price. Only the nominal value of Rs 10 per share is deducted from paid-up capital.
repair.key_idea: Paid-up capital reduces by the nominal value of shares cancelled, not the repurchase price paid by the company.
repair.next_step: Review the definition of paid-up capital and how share repurchases affect it, focusing on nominal vs. repurchase value.
